title: I went to the next parade for the vibes and I sure got them 🤣🏀✨ #newy...
transcript: It's a wonder that Lower Manhattan didn't sink into the ocean today, because it felt like every single person was at the next championship parade. Was it kind of a nightmare? Yes. Did it also remind me why it will always be New York or nowhere? Also, yes. I grew up in the suburbs of New York City, and my dad has been a Knicks fan all of my life. So when dad said he wanted to go to the parade, I was like, we will make this happen. My brothers, also lifetime Knicks fans, don't live in New York anymore, but they came home specifically for this. We got to the access point on Vine and NASA at, like, 6:45, and it was already hopping. And then our dad got trapped, leaving the four or five fold and stop. But eventually he made it over to us, and we tried to get through the barricades, but unfortunately, the pit was full. To be fair, I figured to see the parade, we probably have to get there much earlier, but I was not getting there at four in the morning, and I was very much still enjoying the vibes. And then they ended up letting us pass the first barricade. I thought, we're gonna end up in a prime spot, but there was this garbage truck sitting right here, and one of the sanitation workers did say they were going to move it, but spoiler alert, they don't. But honestly, I was having A great time being there. I love watching my dad. And the biggest miracle is that my friends were able to find me in the crowd. So we all got to hang out and that was really fun. Anyway, back to the garbage truck. There were a lot of let's go Knicks chants, but then there were also a lot of move that truck! Move that truck! Move that truck! The closer we got to 10:00am, the more excited I got. We started to see confetti and I realized that despite the truck, we were gonna have a view of the parade. It's gonna be right here. Mostly look like this, but then occasionally we got to see people when they rode on the double decker buses. So I feel like I did get to experience history a little bit. Most importantly, I got to spend the entire morning with my dad and my brothers and my friends and get to celebrate the greatest city in the world. And now we have the hardware to prove it. After the parade, we wandered around a bit, took in the the atmosphere. I headed home cause I had to work, but my dad and brothers ran into this. But congrats to the New York Knicks. Thanks for bringing us so much joy and kicking summer off in the very best way. Knicks in five.
